title: Fixed Forked Anchor and Tooth Wheel Pendulum Display
description: One newly authored complete fixed anchor-and-tooth-wheel exhibit. A whole grounded plinth and continuous open rear standard support two separate parallel transverse shafts in full bored rings. One entire blunt-tipped radial tooth wheel sits on the lower shaft; a whole forked anchor with two descending arms and opposing end heels is retained on the upper shaft, with a complete long rear rod and low disk bob. The end heels are visibly posed clear of the wheel, not falsely presented as a validated engaged mechanism. Unlike the old open table clock, no dial, hour markers or hands are present; unlike the complete ratchet winch, there is no winding drum, hand crank or independently grounded single pawl. The entire anchor/shaft/rod relationship is newly authored rather than extracted old clockwork or doubled old pawls. Four opaque constant PBR roles, metres, Z up and horizontally centred ground datum. One prop zero scenes. Static illustrative shape only: no escapement action, tooth/pallet profile accuracy, timing, oscillation, winding, power input, rate, engagement, mechanical fit, manufacture, stability, operation or safety performance. Rigging, animation and interaction are not made.
